title: VDR/VER migration progress reporting Q&A/feedback/etc.
author: pete-gov
body:
# VDR/VER Migration Reporting Q&A / General Discussion

On Tue Nov 10, 2026, FedRAMP released [Public Notice NTC-0017 VDR/VER Migration Progress Reporting and Upcoming FY27 Q1 FedRAMP Security Inbox Test](https://www.fedramp.gov/notices/0017/). 

This Notice explained that FedRAMP will be collecting Progress Reports from all FedRAMP Certified cloud service providers who are expected to migrate to the VDR/VER rules and explained how that information will be collected.

It included the [VDR/VER Migration Resources](https://www.fedramp.gov/vdr-migration/) website for additional information on Progress Report collection, including deadlines, corrective action plans, schemas, and more.

---

Collecting progress reports from nearly 600 cloud services is obviously a massive undertaking. We weren't even sure if it was feasible, to be honest. This is partially a test to see how it goes. In the future when folks have adopted CR26 or future consolidated rules things will be much easier as we can simply programmatically monitor everyone's information but today we still need to ask for progress reports.

**This thread is dedicated to questions or feedback about this process, including the content, instructions, schemas, etc.**

comments.author: iteuscher
comments.body:
We noticed that [VDR-TFR-MVF](https://www.fedramp.gov/2026/reference/vulnerability-detection-and-response/#persistent-machine-verification-and-validation-for-rev5) is included as required on the [mini-SDR schema](https://www.fedramp.gov/vdr-migration/assets/implementation-status.schema.json) but the requirement seems only applicable to Rev5 CSPs not 20x CSPs. 

> Persistent Machine Verification and Validation for Rev5
> VDR-TFR-MVF
> Providers of FedRAMP Rev5 Class B/C/D offerings SHOULD/MUST verify and validate the status of machine-based information resources at least once every month.

Should 20x CSPs include VDR-TFR-MVF as Not Applicable in their mini-SDR or leave it out? 

Thanks,
Isaac & Paramify Team

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body: Yes, I intended to put some conditional logic into the JSON schema so [I only flagged this issue for the CSV but woops](https://www.fedramp.gov/vdr-migration/schemas/#not-applicable-rules). Please mark the 20x-specific rule `Not Applicable` (with `capStatus` `Not Applicable`) for Rev5 and vice versa.

comments.author: mmaesc1
comments.body:
Quick sanity check on the Rev5 timing, since the pieces are spread across NTC-0017 and several pages of the migration site. Here’s our reading:

The VDR/VER rules apply December 7, 2026. A Rev5 offering that hasn’t fully migrated owes a per-rule CAP, but nothing gets sent to FedRAMP on December 7 itself.

Between December 1 and 10 (current target December 3), FedRAMP sends the Security Inbox Emergency Test to each certified offering, with its FedRAMP ID and unique code.

That message sets the deadline, anticipated as December 17 at 2pm Eastern. The response goes through the web form and includes the Progress Report Mini-SDR (CSV or JSON). The CAPs are the per-rule CAP fields inside it, with no separate CAP document.

There’s no way to file a Progress Report or CAP before the Emergency Test arrives. Providers should prepare and test early, but filing happens through the test. A VDR/VER CAP sent to FedRAMP some other way before then still has to go in through the Emergency Test.

Is that right?

One piece of feedback: the deadlines table on the site’s front page lists December 7 but not December 17, which is where we got tangled. A row for the Emergency Test there would help.

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body:
> Is that right?

Generally, yes. There's nuance lost in the summary (for example, if we sent out the Emergency Test on December 3 then you **could** choose to submit a progress report before December 7), but it captures the spirit of the game. 

> One piece of feedback: the deadlines table on the site’s front page lists December 7 but not December 17, which is where we got tangled. A row for the Emergency Test there would help.

Ah, I didn't put it here because it's on the [next page down](https://www.fedramp.gov/vdr-migration/emergency-test/), and all the Emergency Test date stuff is subject to change whereas the Important Deadlines on the Overview page were already fixed.

I want folks to plan around those two sets of things separately:

(1) There are deadlines for migrating to the VDR/VER, which are on the overview page. These deadlines are set and extremely unlikely to shift from outside pressure.

(2) There are **expected / anticipated** timeframes for FedRAMP to collect VDR/VER migration progress reports. They might shift, though hopefully the chances of them shifting become less and less as we get closer I can't entirely guarantee it (if CISA orders a data call via Emergency Directive, then we'll have to shift).

That said, if more folks confirm having these dates separate is causing confusion I can revisit the approach.
